system:
You write CANON ENTRIES for an illustrated edition of a work of literature. A canon entry fixes the identity of one character, location or object so that independently generated images agree with each other. Return only JSON matching the schema.

Rules:
- The work's text is binding: anything it says about appearance must be in the entry.
- Where the text is silent, follow the work's widely known visual tradition if one exists; otherwise invent a look that fits the era and the work brief. Never contradict the text.
- Each entry's `text` is one prompt-ready paragraph of at most 500 characters, starting with the name and a colon.
  - character (people, beings, animals, groups): age range; build; skin; hair and beard; facial notes; one signature outfit (the one worn most often) and its colours; signature props the figure carries alone. For a group, describe a typical member.
  - location: terrain; architecture; vegetation; landmarks. No people.
  - object: form; material; colour.
- Fix only identity. Leave out poses, expressions, actions, weather, time of day, other people (attendants, companions, crowds) and anything that compares the figure with someone else.
- STAGES: a character gets more than one stage only when the text itself moves them through childhood, youth, adulthood or old age across the work; a location only when the text marks it built, destroyed or rebuilt. At most three. Objects always have exactly one stage. Each stage is a complete entry on its own.
- Obey the work brief's depiction rules: if a rule limits how this entry may be shown, write only the permitted showing.
- `quotes`: short passages (under 120 characters, copied exactly) the entry relied on, each with the id of the unit it comes from. Only quote units you were given.
- `source`: text, tradition, invention, or mixed.

stages.label: Julia's account of the night whistle
stages.when: The adventure of the speckled band, night of the whistle, before Julia's death
stages.text: Julia's bedroom: a middle room in the old Stoke Moran manor wing, plainly furnished, with a bed, a chair, and a small ventilator set high in the wall near the ceiling. Its heavy shutters open onto the lawn beneath the wing. A bell-rope hangs beside the bed. Ivy and old brick mark the outside; the grounds are flat, wooded and marshy, with a moated ruin and a distant village spire in view. Dim lamp-lit interior, dark wood panelling, faded wallpaper.

quotes.quote: Her room is in the middle, between that of her sister and my own

stages.label: Julia's death and the coroner's findings
stages.when: The adventure of the speckled band, after Julia's death, before Helen's arrival
stages.text: Julia's bedroom: a middle room in the old Stoke Moran manor wing, with a bed, a chair, and a small ventilator set high in the wall near the ceiling, its heavy shutters closed against the night. Dark wood panelling and faded wallpaper; a bell-rope beside the bed. Ivy and aged brick outside; flat, marshy wooded grounds with a moated ruin beyond. Lamp-lit, dim and sombre.

quotes.quote: the door was locked upon the inside, and the windows fastened

stages.label: Examination of the outside of the wing and the shutters
stages.when: The adventure of the speckled band, Holmes's investigation of the exterior
stages.text: Julia's bedroom exterior: the outside wall of the old manor wing, ivy-covered aged brick, with a window set beneath heavy shutters and a ventilator opening high in the wall. Flat, marshy wooded grounds, a lawn beneath the wing, and a moated ruin beyond. Dim dawn or dusk light, muted greens and browns, no people.

quotes.quote: the shutters folded back against the wall

stages.label: Inspection of Julia's bedroom: the bell-rope and ventilator
stages.when: The adventure of the speckled band, Holmes's inspection of the room
stages.text: Julia's bedroom: a middle room in the old Stoke Moran manor wing, with a bed, a chair, and a bell-rope hanging beside it that ends in air. A small ventilator is set high in the wall near the ceiling, its opening connected to the room beyond. Dark wood panelling, faded wallpaper, dim lamp-lit interior, a sombre and worn character.

stages.when: The adventure of the speckled band, Holmes's preparations for the vigil
stages.text: Julia's bedroom: a middle room in the old Stoke Moran manor wing, with a bed, a chair, and a small ventilator high in the wall near the ceiling. Dark wood panelling and faded wallpaper; a bell-rope beside the bed. Heavy shutters, ivy and aged brick outside; flat, marshy wooded grounds with a moated ruin beyond. Dim lamp-lit interior, sombre and gothic.

quotes.quote: the room in which she was sleeping

stages.label: The vigil in darkness
stages.when: The adventure of the speckled band, the night of the vigil in darkness
stages.text: Julia's bedroom in darkness: a middle room in the old Stoke Moran manor wing, with a bed, a chair, and a small ventilator high in the wall near the ceiling. Dark wood panelling and faded wallpaper, lit only by a dark-lantern or moonlight through the shutters. Bell-rope beside the bed. Gothic and suspenseful; no people.

stages.label: The snake, Roylott's death and its discovery
stages.when: The adventure of the speckled band, the night of the snake and Roylott's death
stages.text: Julia's bedroom in the old Stoke Moran manor wing: a middle room with a bed, a chair, and a small ventilator high in the wall near the ceiley, its opening leading to the room beyond. Dark wood panelling, faded wallpaper, a bell-rope beside the bed. Dim lamp-lit gothic interior, sombre and still. No people.
